transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Marcus Chen (Orchid - Head of ML), Ayesha Patel (Orchid - SRE), Liam Gomez (Orchid - CTO)

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and how Redwood surfaces cost attribution. Customer is evaluating tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated for latency/cost; security questions (VPC, SOC2) came up. Agreed next steps: share pricing, security pack, and run a short benchmark on Dedicated if Orchid provides typical workload.

Topics: per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, route tagging, rollouts, caching impact on cost, dedicated vs hosted economics, SSO/KMS, POC benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 40 minutes, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our Solutions Engineer. quick intro?
[00:22] Marcus: Yeah hi Marcus here, I lead ML at Orchid Medical. we'll be evaluating inference for our clinical summarization and triage flows. main concerns are latency for triage, and cost for bulk summarization.
[00:45] Ayesha: Ayesha, SRE. network constraints and audit logs are my focus, and we need to know what we can lock down in our VPC.
[01:05] Liam: Liam, CTO, quick oversight. interested in whether Dedicated gives us predictable unit costs vs hosted.
[01:22] Jordan: Great, that's exactly what we'll show. Priya will walk through the Console analytics and cost views; I'll jump in on pricing and deployment options. Caveat - demo is a console walkthrough, not a full POC yet.
[01:45] Priya: Alright pulling up the Console, you should see the per-route dashboard. note this is a demo org so numbers are synthetic. first card is usage over time, second is latency distribution, third is cost-by-route.
[02:10] Priya: (points) You can tag routes by regex or route name, so for you "triage" vs "summarize" routes can be split. cost attribution is token-level so we show prompt vs completion tokens and GPU time estimate.
[02:35] Marcus: How accurate is the GPU time estimate? we run mixed seq lengths - the average is like 60 tokens but triage sometimes spikes.
[02:50] Priya: Good question. estimate is based on runtime profiles per model variant; it uses recent seq-distribution and kernel profiles. it's an estimate but typically within 10-15% for similar workloads. we also support exporting raw per-request timing if you want exact benchmarking.
[03:15] Ayesha: For auditability do you keep logs with token counts and inputs? we can't send PHI to hosted endpoints without controls.
[03:30] Jordan: We have Private deployments + Dedicated. Private allows customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem. We also provide KMS integrations and audit logs. I'll attach SOC 2 and the security pack after the call.
[03:50] Marcus: Ok - if we go Dedicated, does Redwood still provide the observability console or is that local?
[04:05] Priya: Observability is available in both modes. For Private the Console can be routed through the customer's control plane; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. some customers prefer the Console in read-only mode behind the VPC.
[04:25] Liam: Walk me through cost by route - we need to bill back to product teams. can we break down cost per endpoint and per-customer?
[04:40] Priya: Yes - per-route dashboards support tags, and you can map routes to billing codes. Example: triage-route -> product-team-a. The cost card supports grouping by route, model, or tag. exportable CSV includes token counts, estimated GPU seconds, and cost allocation.
[05:05] Marcus: Do you do prefix/KV caching? for summarization a lot of inputs share templates, would that cut cost significantly?
[05:20] Priya: Yes, we have automatic prefix and KV cache. For summarization you typically see 20-60% token savings depending on prefix reuse. Console shows cache hit ratio and token savings per route.
[05:45] Jordan: On the pricing side: hosted is usage-based per token and embedding unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity with committed throughput and lower per-token cost. we'll send a sample cost sheet showing break-even points given your expected QPS and sequence lengths.
[06:10] Marcus: What's a typical break-even QPS?
[06:20] Jordan: It depends on seq length and percent of streaming vs batch. as a rule of thumb - if you need sustained throughput above ~10-15 rps with small seqs, Dedicated can be cheaper. We'll model this in the spreadsheet.
[06:40] Ayesha: Network - if we use Dedicated inside our VPC do we need specific egress rules? our firewall is pretty locked down.
[06:54] Priya: For Private Dedicated with VPC we provide required endpoints and ports in the security pack. Usually you just need to allow outbound to the control plane and syslog endpoints. we'll list exact CIDR ranges.
[07:10] Liam: Any customers in healthcare doing PHI? curious how Redwood handles data residency and retention.
[07:25] Jordan: Yes, a few healthcare customers use Private deployments and on-prem. retention policies are configurable, and KMS/HSM for keys. We'll include a brief case note in the security pack.
[07:45] Marcus: Back to console: can we create alerts when cost for a route spikes? say summarization suddenly uses a new model and costs double.
[08:00] Priya: Absolutely - per-route alerts and regression detection are supported. You can set cost thresholds, token-per-request thresholds, and quality regressions tied to evals. We'll show alert config later in the POC.
[08:20] Ayesha: How granular is the token accounting - do you split prompt vs generation? we need to allocate costs for customer-supplied prompts separately.
[08:34] Priya: Yes split shown as prompt vs completion tokens. For streaming requests it's accounted incrementally. The export includes columns for prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, model_variant, and estimated gpu_ms.
[08:55] Marcus: Are function calls represented separately? we have a lot of tool-calls which should be considered overhead not direct model cost.
[09:10] Priya: We surface tool-call counts and approximate cost impact. If you do heavy tool-calling we recommend moving non-LLM logic to downstream services and instrumenting calls for cost tags.
[09:30] Jordan: Quick demo of the cost breakdown panel - (screen share) here we filter to "summarize" tag. you can see 7-day trends, moving average cost per thousand tokens, and contributors: model, route, and cache misses.
[09:55] Priya: You can also create a per-route SLA with latency SLOs. Console overlays latency percentiles with cost so you can tune batch size vs P99.
[10:15] Marcus: We need P99 < 200ms for triage. is that achievable on 8k context?
[10:29] Priya: For triage with short seqs P99 < 200ms is achievable on Dedicated with optimized kernels; hosted can do it too but Dedicated gives stronger guarantees since autoscaling is tuned to committed capacity.
[10:50] Ayesha: Clarify autoscaling - will Dedicated autoscale within the reserved pool or spin up new hardware?
[11:02] Priya: Autoscaling happens within the reserved pool; for burst we have configurable burst capacity that can pull from shared capacity if enabled. Policies are configurable per-route.
[11:20] Liam: What about model variants and rollouts - can we do canary that falls back if latency or cost spikes?
[11:32] Priya: Yes rollouts support weighted routing, canary, and automatic fallback. Console shows comparative metrics side-by-side. If a canary increases cost by X% we can auto-fallback.
[11:52] Marcus: Example: we want to test a cheaper quantized variant for summarization; how to ensure quality doesn't regress?
[12:05] Priya: Tie your evals to rollouts - you can run golden prompts set and track quality metrics. Console will alert on quality regression thresholds and you can abort rollout automatically.
[12:25] Jordan: I'll note that Redwood Optimize sends model and quant suggestions based on workload. Priya, show the per-route recommendations card.
[12:38] Priya: (navigating) optimize suggests batching sizes, quant profiles, and whether to switch model family. it gives estimated monthly savings per recommendation. this ties directly into the cost card.
[12:58] Ayesha: Any limitations around HIPAA?
[13:10] Jordan: We can't give legal advice but many healthcare customers use Private deployments + dedicated key management and have contracts to support HIPAA. we'll include compliance FAQ and reference architectures.
[13:30] Marcus: For the benchmark we want to run our triage workload and compare latency/cost hosted vs Dedicated. do you have a template?
[13:45] Priya: Yes we'll provide a benchmarking template (script + payloads). if you share typical QPS and sequences we'll provision a small Dedicated cluster for a week for benchmarking.
[14:05] Liam: Cost modeling: can you show an example of how the spreadsheet looks?
[14:18] Jordan: (posts link in chat) here's a sample cost model - columns: route, avg_seq_len, qps, cache_hit_rate, estimated_gpu_seconds, hosted_cost, dedicated_cost, break-even month. we'll pre-fill with your numbers once you share them.
[14:40] Marcus: About tags - can we map to internal chargeback codes? we have product codes like ORCH-ML-TRIAGE.
[14:50] Priya: Yes tags are flexible key/value and can be synced with your internal billing system via CSV export or API.
[15:05] Ayesha: We use SAML SSO and Okta; any issues?
[15:15] Jordan: We support SAML/Okta and RBAC. For Private you can centralize provisioning. details in the security pack.
[15:28] Marcus: Data residency - European customers we need region pinning.
[15:38] Priya: Region pinning is supported. For Private we can deploy in your preferred region or on-prem.
[15:50] Liam: Anything you want from us to get a POC going?
[16:00] Jordan: We'll need: expected QPS per route, avg and 95th seq lengths, sample payloads (anonymized), and network constraints. Ayesha, you'll own the firewall info?
[16:14] Ayesha: Yes I'll gather firewall rules and any compliance questions, send by next week.
[16:25] Marcus: Timeline - we aim to decide by end of March if POC viable.
[16:34] Jordan: Sounds good. we'll aim to get pricing and security pack to you in 48 hours. Priya will prepare the benchmark template.
[16:50] Priya: Quick note - console also has anomaly detection for sudden cost spikes and a per-route changelog for model/version changes.
[17:05] Marcus: Great. about the per-request export - can we pull raw JSON with token counts? our finance team wants verbatim rows.
[17:18] Priya: yes full export available via UI and API; retention configurable. we can show you the CSV format in the POC.
[17:35] Ayesha: If we do Dedicated, what does maintenance look like? patches, upgrades?
[17:48] Priya: Redwood handles runtime patches; for Private we coordinate maintenance windows with you. Dedicated nodes can accept rolling upgrades to avoid downtime.
[18:02] Liam: Any hard limits on route count or tags?
[18:12] Priya: No hard limits; we recommend sane tag conventions. Route cardinality can be scaled but extremely high cardinality can affect dashboard performance - we can advise on aggregation.
[18:30] Marcus: Okay last thing - are there native integrations to Datadog / Splunk for metric forwarding?
[18:42] Priya: Yes metrics and logs can be forwarded to Datadog, Splunk, Cloudwatch, or your SIEM.
[19:00] Jordan: Recap of next steps: I'll email pricing and SOC 2 pack; Priya will share benchmark template and cost spreadsheet; Ayesha will send network requirements and any compliance Qs. follow-up POC scoping for week of 2026-03-16.
[19:25] Liam: Thanks everyone, this was useful.
[19:30] Marcus: Thanks, talk soon.

Note: Transcript has imperfect speaker attribution in places and occasional transcription errors (e.g., "KV cahce" instead of "KV cache"). Links shared during call: [Pricing spreadsheet], [Security pack - SOC 2 + KMS details], [Benchmark template].

End of meeting.
